method: Separate named eddy families and recurring geographic names from source-dated individuals. Regional locators are editorial gateways; dated study centers and core-water CTD stations retain their distinct evidence types. A study center is not a closed footprint or NASA ECCO identity. Do not infer OSW state containment from these points.

entries.name: Batumi Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial southeastern Black Sea point offshore of Batumi; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Bosphorus Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial Black Sea point north of the Bosphorus; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Sukhumi Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial northeastern Black Sea point offshore of Sukhumi; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Caucasus Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial eastern Black Sea point near the Caucasus coast; not a dated eddy center or an alias for Marine Regions' Caucasus Current.

entries.name: Kerch Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial Black Sea point south of Kerch Strait; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Crimea Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial Black Sea point south of Crimea; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Sevastopol Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial Black Sea point southwest of Sevastopol; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Danube Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial northwestern Black Sea point offshore of the Danube delta; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Constantsa Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial western Black Sea point offshore of Constanța; spelling follows the cited paper, not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Kaliakra Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial western Black Sea point east of Cape Kaliakra; not a dated eddy center.

entries.name: Haida eddies
entries.locator_basis: Editorial formation-region point west of Haida Gwaii; not an observed individual center.

entries.name: Sitka eddies
entries.locator_basis: Editorial formation-region point offshore of Sitka; not an observed individual center.

entries.name: Yakutat eddies
entries.locator_basis: Editorial formation-region point southeast of Yakutat; not an observed individual center.

entries.name: Kenai eddies
entries.locator_basis: Editorial point in the paper's proposed formation area south of the Kenai Peninsula; not a documented center or a claim that every generation follows one path.

entries.name: Agulhas Rings
entries.locator_basis: Editorial gateway near the Agulhas retroflection where NASA describes ring shedding; not a single ring center or footprint.

independent_source_census.definition_note: The 74 are long-lived tracks after ring dissipation, splitting, and merging; they are not 74 individually named rings and are not NASA ECCO eddy identities.

entries.name: Agulhas Ring Astrid
entries.locator_basis: Study-reported center of ring Astrid during the March 2000 MARE-1 cruise; not a ring footprint or a position in NASA's 2021–2023 film.

observed_center.method: satellite sea-surface-height anomaly with ship survey
observed_center.note: The study gives 37°30′S, 18°E for Astrid's center during MARE-1; ring boundaries and track are not digitized here.

formation.note: Pinched off near 38°S, 17°30′E according to the study.

entries.reported_radius_definition: Radius at maximum tangential velocity, from the source two-layer circularly symmetric ring model. Not an outer eddy boundary.

radial_scale_evidence.name: Agulhas Ring Astrid
radial_scale_evidence.definition: Radius at maximum tangential velocity, from the source two-layer circularly symmetric ring model. Not an outer eddy boundary.
radial_scale_evidence.layer: Two-layer diagnostic model whose thermocline follows the 10 C isotherm; primarily baroclinic component. Lower layer assumed at rest; actual LADCP flow extended to the bottom.
radial_scale_evidence.source_locator: Table 3, printed p. 191 (PDF page 25), Astrid row and footnotes b / final model note.

radial_scale_evidence.name: Agulhas Ring Astrid
radial_scale_evidence.definition: Chosen integration limit where thermocline depth relaxes to surrounding value; not a mapped observed closed perimeter.
radial_scale_evidence.layer: Two-layer diagnostic model whose thermocline follows the 10 C isotherm; primarily baroclinic component. Lower layer assumed at rest; actual LADCP flow extended to the bottom.
radial_scale_evidence.source_locator: Section 7.2, printed p. 191 (PDF page 25), paragraph immediately preceding Table 3 discussion.

entries.name: Agulhas Ring Laura
entries.locator_basis: Study-reported March 2000 sea-surface-height anomaly center for ring Laura; the authors caution that the hydrographic center differed. This is not a closed footprint or a NASA-era position.

observed_center.note: The study gives 37°S, 14°15′E from SSH anomaly and says the hydrographic center differed, probably after recent movement.

formation.note: Shed near 38°S, 18°E according to the study.

entries.name: Agulhas Ring Ana
entries.locator_basis: Study-reported first detected center on 15 August 2004; later trans-Atlantic path is shown in the paper but is not digitized here. This point is not a closed footprint or a NASA-era position.

observed_center.note: First detected center, 38.26°S/17.10°E; the study follows the ring to 9 May 2007 near 33°W, without a digitized footprint in this ledger.

entries.name: Agulhas Ring Eliza
entries.locator_basis: Approximate study-reported split-off position near 38°S/16°E about one month after the parent ring shed on 1 August 2007; this is an event-region point, not a measured eddy center, closed footprint, or NASA-era position.

formation.note: Split-off from a ring shed from the retroflection on 1 August 2007; the source's 1,007-day track counts from the parent-ring shedding, not necessarily Eliza's independent lifetime.

reported_track_period.scope: source track from parent-ring shedding through Eliza's reported demise; not an unbroken individual lifetime

entries.name: Agulhas Ring Jeannette
entries.locator_basis: Study-reported track starting point on 28 January 2012 at 39°S/17°E. This is not a closed footprint or a NASA-era position; the track's identity across a later merger is method-dependent.

observed_center.note: Starting point of the source's Jeannette track; it ends 27 December 2015 near 21°S/35°W.

additional_observed_positions.note: The study reports the track finishing at 21°S, 35°W. This point is not a measured footprint; the tracked identity spans a merger and depends on the tracking method.

entries.identity_note: This study's Ring Jeannette track spans a merger. It says Nencioli et al. (2018) instead label its pre-merger southern track AS2 and post-merger ring B12, with northern contributing track AN1. Those are source-scoped track identifiers, not three additional personal ring names or proven continuous identities.

entries.name: Agulhas Ring Lilian
entries.locator_basis: Study Figure 3(a) reports Ring Lilian's positive sea-level anomaly near 25.5°S, 38°W on 7 June 2006; approximate center from the caption, not a digitized contour or full track.

observed_center.note: Approximate figure-caption position; the authors also identify Chelton global eddy track 147078 as Lilian.

additional_observed_positions.note: The study reports Ring Lilian was first detected at 39.5°S, 14.6°E, but gives no date in this passage. This is a point, not a complete ring track or footprint.

external_track_identifier.evidence: The study explicitly identifies Lilian with track label 147078; this has not been independently rejoined to a downloadable track in OSW.

reported_encounter.place: Brazil Current margin south of Cape Frio
reported_encounter.evidence: Study reports passage of Lilian's northern edge over a mooring line; this does not locate the ring center or prove whole-ring containment.

entries.identity_note: The study reports more than 5,500 km of travel over about 3.5 years before the ring's signal faded near 30°S. Lilian is a named historical Agulhas ring, not an individual object identified in NASA's 2021–2023 model film.
entries.reported_motion_source_locator: PDF page 7, paragraph before Section 4 Conclusions (3.5-year lifetime and journey of more than 5,500 km); Section 3.2 and Figure 1 identify Ring Lilian

entries.name: Agulhas Eddy W
entries.locator_basis: Published station 06 at 29.2°S, 8.2°E sampled the center of eddy W on 22 February 2000; this is a dated sampled center, not a closed footprint or complete trajectory.

observed_center.method: TOPEX/Poseidon sea-surface-height image plus MARE station 06 CTD and plankton sampling
observed_center.note: The source says the ring center lay at station 06 during the 22 February sampling; Table 1 gives 29.2°S, 8.2°E.

entries.identity_note: The publication uses W as a source-scoped individual eddy label. It reports visibility in October 1999, a centered sample in February 2000, and disappearance from sea-surface-height images in May 2000. Image disappearance is not a proven physical death. No source-backed identity match to Astrid or Laura or to NASA's later model film is asserted.

entries.name: Peddies (Persian Gulf Water eddies)
entries.locator_basis: Midpoint of the 2021–2022 glider transect (24.05–24.5°N, 57.5–57.8°E) where off-shelf Persian Gulf Water patches were sampled; not a peddy center, footprint, or surface signal.
entries.vertical_evidence: Subsurface Persian Gulf Water patches sampled by gliders; the study reports no sea-surface-height signature for peddies.

entries.name: Cuba anticyclones (CubANs)
entries.basin: Southern Gulf of Mexico / northwestern Cuba
entries.locator_basis: Editorial northwestern Cuba gateway to the southern Gulf study area; the paper reports five activity periods during 2010, not a single eddy center, footprint, or NASA-era individual.
entries.identity_note: CubANs are a study-defined class of southern Gulf anticyclones, distinct from the individually named 2010 Loop Current ring Franklin. NASA describes Gulf loop eddies generically and does not identify CubANs.

entries.name: Haida-1998
entries.locator_basis: Formation-region gateway off Haida Gwaii, not the studied 1998 eddy's dated center or footprint.

entries.name: Sitka Eddy (2007)
entries.locator_basis: Published CTD cast 6 sampled water classified as the 2007 Sitka Eddy core on 22 August 2007; a core-water station is not the eddy center or footprint.

reported_fate.note: The study reports dissipation in early December 2007; this is not a precise lifetime.

entries.name: Kenai Eddy (2007)
entries.locator_basis: Published CTD cast 47 sampled water classified as the 2007 Kenai Eddy core on 8 September 2007; a core-water station is not the eddy center or footprint.

reported_fate.note: Still present at the last available altimetry observation in the study; the final dissipation date is unknown.

entries.name: Meddies (Mediterranean Water eddies)
entries.basin: Eastern North Atlantic / Gulf of Cadiz
entries.locator_basis: Editorial Gulf of Cadiz formation-region gateway near the Mediterranean Undercurrent; not a meddy center, surface signature, or footprint.
entries.vertical_evidence: Meddies are warm, saline subsurface lenses formed from Mediterranean outflow; a NASA geographic crop alone does not verify a visible meddy at depth.

entries.name: Meddy Ulla
entries.locator_basis: Ulla study reports a ship-discovered meddy at 45°N, 11°30′W in April 1997; this is a source position, not a closed lens footprint or NASA-era identity.

observed_center.note: The published discovery position is approximate; the study describes a warm, saline core near 1,000 m and observations in 1997–1998.

entries.vertical_evidence: Ulla's defining warm, saline core was near 1,000 m depth; the NASA regional crop is a geographic view, not visual confirmation of this historical subsurface eddy.

entries.name: Cyprus Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial point southwest of Cyprus within the recurring eddy region described by the 2012 drifter and altimetry study; not a dated center or boundary.
entries.identity_note: The study reports variable Cyprus Eddy activity and periods when it enlarges to include the Shikmona Eddy. This is a recurring name, not one persistent individual.

entries.name: Shikmona Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial offshore Israel-Lebanon point in the southeastern Levantine region analyzed by the 2012 drifter and altimetry study; not a dated center or boundary.
entries.identity_note: The study finds stronger Shikmona Eddy activity in cold months and during 1998–2005. The regional name covers recurring activity, not a single lifetime.

entries.name: Latakia Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Editorial offshore Syrian-coast point near Latakia in the region analyzed by the 2012 drifter and altimetry study; not a dated center or boundary.
entries.identity_note: The study describes the Latakia Eddy as mainly cyclonic, stronger in summer and fall, with occasional weekly or monthly anticyclonic reversals. One fixed polarity would hide that variability.

entries.name: Mindanao Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Approximate recurring center reported near 7°N, 128°E; a typical center is not a dated observation or closed footprint.
entries.identity_note: A quasi-permanent circulation associated with the western Pacific North Equatorial Countercurrent meander; the regional name does not denote one persistent individually tracked vortex.

entries.name: Halmahera Eddy
entries.locator_basis: Approximate recurring center reported near 3°–4°N, 131°E; a typical center is not a dated observation or closed footprint.
entries.identity_note: A quasi-permanent circulation associated with the western Pacific North Equatorial Countercurrent meander; its study-defined activity box is not an individual eddy outline or NASA identity.

entries.name: New Guinea Eddy
entries.basin: Western equatorial Pacific north of New Guinea
entries.locator_basis: Editorial point near the approximately 2°N, 138°E intermediate-depth variability site discussed in the 2017 observation abstract; not a dated eddy center or closed footprint.
entries.vertical_evidence: The 2017 study discusses this anticyclonic eddy in 300–750 m intermediate-depth variability; a surface NASA crop cannot verify its subsurface structure.
entries.identity_note: Grenier et al. label a New Guinea Eddy in their western Pacific schematic; the 2017 intermediate-depth study also uses New Guinea Eddy. A 2019 paper calls an anticyclonic feature near 136°E 'North Guinea Eddy' (NGE). The spellings and positions are retained as source-specific observations rather than treated as a verified individual identity match.
